title: Attendance & absences
sourceRightsNote: Synthetic content created for the PolicyLens demo.
summary: A small, clearly labelled policy excerpt for demonstrating grounded answers.

chunks.text: A parent or guardian should notify the school before 9:00 a.m. on a day the student will be absent.
chunks.answer: For an absence, a parent or guardian should notify the school before 9:00 a.m. that morning.
chunks.nextStep: If your school uses a different reporting channel, confirm it with the attendance office.
chunks.exampleQuestion: What should I do if I will be absent?

chunks.text: Students should bring an absence note to the attendance office within three school days of returning.
chunks.answer: After returning, bring an absence note to the attendance office within three school days.
chunks.nextStep: Keep a copy of the note if your school asks for documentation.
chunks.exampleQuestion: Where do I bring an absence note?

title: Personal devices
sourceRightsNote: Synthetic content created for the PolicyLens demo.
summary: A synthetic device rule used to test evidence and not-found behavior.

chunks.text: Personal phones and smart devices should be silenced and kept in a student bag during lessons unless a teacher gives permission.
chunks.answer: During lessons, keep personal phones and smart devices silenced and in your bag unless your teacher gives permission.
chunks.nextStep: Ask the teacher before using a personal device during a lesson.
chunks.exampleQuestion: What should I do with my phone during class?

chunks.text: A student may use a device for an approved medical or accessibility need after arranging a plan with the school.
chunks.answer: Approved medical or accessibility needs can be supported through a plan arranged with the school.
chunks.nextStep: Arrange the support plan with the school before relying on the exception.
chunks.exampleQuestion: When can I use a device for accessibility?

title: Accessibility & support
sourceRightsNote: Synthetic content created for the PolicyLens demo.
summary: A synthetic support guide for demonstrating accommodation-related questions.

chunks.text: Students and families can contact the school support team to discuss an accessibility plan for classroom participation.
chunks.answer: Students and families can contact the school support team to discuss an accessibility plan for classroom participation.
chunks.nextStep: Contact the school support team to discuss the student’s specific needs.
chunks.exampleQuestion: Who can discuss an accessibility plan with my family?

chunks.text: The support team can review an accessibility plan when a student’s classroom needs change.
chunks.answer: The support team can review an accessibility plan when classroom needs change.
chunks.nextStep: Ask the support team for a review when the student’s needs change.
chunks.exampleQuestion: When can a support plan be reviewed?
